neighbours.label: Anticipates a written or alternative communication form at a conjunction or preposition following spoken, oral or verbal expression.
fire: The assessment measures a candidate's oral and written fluency in the second language.
All complaints may be delivered verbally or in a signed statement.
Staff must explain the procedure both in speech and on paper.
The historian compared the community's spoken and recorded accounts of the event.
The counselor accepts concerns expressed orally or through a letter.
The policy treats verbal and written promises as equally serious commitments.
Children practice describing their observations in spoken and written form.
The agreement can be communicated by word of mouth or in writing.
quiet: The assessment measures a candidate's reading and handwriting skills in the second language.
Each complaint must arrive as a signed statement before the office closes.
Staff must explain the procedure clearly and patiently to every new employee.
The historian compared the community's printed and handwritten accounts of the event.
The counselor accepts letters submitted personally or through the post.
The policy treats public and private promises as equally serious commitments.
Children practice describing their observations using pictures and diagrams.
The agreement was written on a standard form and placed in the office records.

notes: Strong peaks precede writing rather than occur on written itself. The same spoken-and prefix fired before both written and recorded, so the hypothesis concerns the predictive context, not the later word. Near misses vary the lead-in and include writing without the speech contrast.
